title: What is telephony? A guide for small businesses
summary: Learn what telephony is, the types that exist today, and how cloud telephony helps small businesses stay responsive and connected.
body_markdown:
Telephony is the technology that transmits voice communication over a distance — and for small businesses, it's often the backbone of every customer call, team check-in, and sales follow-up you make. For most of the 20th century, telephony meant a wired landline connected to the public switched telephone network (PSTN). But today, the category has expanded to include mobile, internet, and cloud-based systems that are faster to set up, cheaper to run, and far more capable than the copper-wire systems they've replaced. If you're evaluating your business phone setup — or just trying to understand the terminology — this guide breaks down how telephony works, what the main types are, and what small businesses should be thinking about in 2026.

## Telephony definition


Telephony is the technology and systems used to transmit voice (and sometimes data) between two or more people over a distance. It covers the hardware, software, and network infrastructure that make real-time voice communication possible — from analog desk phones to cloud-based business phone systems.


## How telephony works


At its core, telephony converts sound into a signal, transmits that signal across a network, and converts it back into sound at the other end. The way that conversion and transmission happens has changed significantly over time.


Traditional telephony uses physical copper wires and circuit switching — a dedicated connection is opened between two callers for the duration of the call. Modern internet telephony, by contrast, converts voice into digital data packets and sends them across the internet, a technology known as voice over internet protocol (VoIP). Cloud telephony takes this further by hosting the entire phone system — the switching, routing, and features — in the cloud rather than on hardware in your office.


## Types of telephony


Not all telephony works the same way. Here's a breakdown of the four main types and what distinguishes them.


### Traditional (PSTN) telephony


The public switched telephone network, or PSTN, is the original landline system. Calls travel through physical copper lines and circuit-switched exchanges. PSTN is reliable and widely understood, but it's also expensive to maintain, difficult to scale, and increasingly being replaced by newer technology.


### Mobile telephony


Mobile telephony transmits voice calls wirelessly through cellular networks (such as 4G and 5G). It's the foundation of every smartphone call. For small businesses, mobile telephony is often used alongside a business phone system so employees can use a professional number from their personal device.


### Internet telephony (VoIP)


Internet telephony — most commonly called VoIP — converts voice into digital packets and routes them over the internet. VoIP is the basis for many modern business phone systems. It's flexible, cost-effective, and supports features that traditional PSTN simply can't: call routing, voicemail transcription, auto attendants, and AI-powered call features.


### Fax telephony


Fax telephony transmits documents over phone lines, converting them into audio signals for transmission. While fax usage has declined significantly, it remains relevant in regulated industries like healthcare and legal, where fax is still a standard for sending sensitive documents.


### Telephony comparison: traditional vs. mobile vs. internet


Feature Traditional (PSTN) Mobile Internet (VoIP/cloud)


**Infrastructure** Copper wires, on-premise hardware Cellular towers Internet connection


**Setup complexity** High Low Low


**Cost** Higher (lines, hardware, maintenance) Medium Lower (software-based)


**Scalability** Difficult Limited Easy


**AI features** Typically none Limited Yes (call summary, voicemail prioritization, etc.)


**Works on mobile** No Yes Yes


## Telephony vs. VoIP: what's the difference?


"Telephony" is the broad category — it covers any technology used to transmit voice over a distance, including landlines, mobile networks, and the internet. VoIP, or voice over internet protocol, is a specific type of telephony that routes calls over the internet instead of dedicated phone lines. When people say "business VoIP," they typically mean a cloud-based phone system that runs on your internet connection. Learn more about[what VoIP is and how it works](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/what-is-voip/) .


## Why telephony matters for small businesses


For a small business, your phone system is often the first touchpoint a customer has with your brand. A dropped call, a busy signal, or a voicemail that never gets checked can cost you a customer — and in a competitive market, that matters.


Modern cloud telephony addresses three core problems SMBs face:


**Cost.** Traditional PBX systems (private branch exchange) require expensive hardware and dedicated IT support to maintain. Cloud telephony runs on your existing internet connection. Many providers offer pay-per-user plans with no long-term hardware commitment.


**Flexibility.** Your team doesn't all work from the same desk anymore. Cloud telephony lets you answer calls on a desk phone, a laptop, or your mobile device — using the same business number. Shared lines and call groups mean customers reach someone, even when you're out.


**Features.** Cloud systems offer capabilities that would have required enterprise-level hardware just a decade ago: call routing, auto attendants, call queues, SMS, voicemail transcription, and AI-powered summaries that capture what was said after calls.


If you're still running a[VoIP vs. landline](https://www.zoom.com/en/blog/voip-vs-landline/) comparison for your business, the short answer for many SMBs is that cloud telephony offers more value, more flexibility, and a lower cost of ownership.

## Frequently asked questions about telephony


### What is telephony in simple terms?


Telephony is the technology that lets people communicate by voice over a distance. It covers everything from old-fashioned landline phones to modern cloud-based business phone systems that run over the internet.


### What are the different types of telephony?


The four main types are traditional (PSTN) telephony using copper landlines, mobile telephony over cellular networks, internet telephony (VoIP) over broadband, and fax telephony for document transmission. Most modern business phone systems are built on VoIP or cloud telephony.


### What is the difference between VoIP and telephony?


Telephony is the broad category for any voice communication technology. VoIP, which stands for voice over internet protocol, is a specific type of telephony that routes calls over the internet rather than a traditional phone line. VoIP is now the foundation of most business phone systems.


### What is internet telephony used for?


Internet telephony is used for business phone calls, video conferencing, messaging, and collaboration. Small businesses use it to manage customer calls, support remote and hybrid teams, run call queues and auto attendants, and connect their phone system with CRM and productivity tools.


### Is telephony the same as a phone system?


Not exactly. Telephony refers to the underlying technology and infrastructure that enables voice communication. A business phone system — like Zoom Phone — is a product built on telephony technology, typically adding features like call routing, voicemail, shared lines, and integrations.

## Conclusion


Telephony has evolved from copper-wire landlines to cloud-based systems that work across any device, integrate with your business tools, and use AI to help you stay on top of every customer interaction.
